arguments.summary: Rename `signed` parameter of number converters to `allow_negative`, but incomplete updates leave tests and docstrings referencing the old name.

findings.explanation: The pull request renames the `signed` parameter to `allow_negative` in `NumberConverter`, `IntegerConverter`, and `FloatConverter`, but leaves the test suite (`tests/test_routing.py`) and docstring parameter descriptions using the old `signed` keyword argument. This will cause `TypeError` / test failures when running tests that pass `signed=True`.
findings.suggested_fix: Update tests/test_routing.py to use `allow_negative=True` and update the docstrings in converters.py to document `allow_negative` instead of `signed`.
findings.claim: Tests and docstrings still reference the old parameter name `signed` instead of `allow_negative`, causing test failure or outdated documentation.

evidence.note: tests test_negative uses int(signed=True) and float(signed=True) which was renamed to allow_negative
IntegerConverter docstring still refers to parameter `signed` instead of `allow_negative`
FloatConverter docstring still refers to parameter `signed` instead of `allow_negative`
